in-caridina-multidentata.title: Amano Shrimp
in-caridina-multidentata.summary: A hardy algae-grazing shrimp popularized by Takashi Amano. Larger than cherry shrimp and will not flood a freshwater tank with babies.
rows: Small to large planted tanks with a tight lid
Peaceful; may bully smaller shrimp off food pellets
Scavenger. Soft algae, biofilm, dead plant matter, wafers, blanched greens, leftover fish food
notes: Larvae need brackish/salt water — no freshwater colony boom.
Leave molts in the tank so shrimp can reclaim minerals.

in-neocaridina-davidi.title: Neocaridina Dwarf Shrimp
in-neocaridina-davidi.summary: Colorful dwarf shrimp that breed in freshwater. Excellent clean-up crew for planted tanks when fish will not eat the shrimplets.
rows: Females to about 1.5 in (4 cm); males smaller
Nanos work; 10 gal+ is better for breeding. Sponge-filter or prefilter the intake
Peaceful; almost any fish will eat babies
Biofilm, algae, leftover foods, blanched veg, calcium-rich shrimp foods
About 6.5–8.5 with enough GH/KH for clean molts
China and Taiwan; ornamental morphs are captive-bred
notes: A clear split shell is usually a molt, not a corpse.

in-atyopsis-mollucensis.title: Bamboo Shrimp (Fan Shrimp)
in-atyopsis-mollucensis.sci: Atyopsis moluccensis (also sold as A. gabonensis / wood shrimp)
in-atyopsis-mollucensis.summary: A filter-feeding freshwater shrimp that fans particulate food from the water with setae on its claws. Needs steady flow and fine foods; peaceful with shrimp-safe tankmates.
rows: About 20 gal or larger with good flow
Filter feeder — needs suspended fine foods (powdered foods, bacterioplankton products); will not thrive on pellets alone if flow is poor
Southeast Asia (A. moluccensis); African listings may be A. gabonensis
notes: Catalog may list Atyopsis gabonensis or mollucensis — care is similar for fan shrimp in the trade.

in-procambarus-clarkii.title: Red Swamp Crayfish (Ghost, Snow White, Tangerine, Tricolor)
in-procambarus-clarkii.summary: The Louisiana crawfish, sold here in captive color forms. Hardy and bold, but it digs, shreds plants and eats tankmates, so keep it alone in a covered tank.
rows: About 4–5 in long; big males reach about 6 in
20 gal long for one adult (30 gal long is better)
Aggressive, predatory loner: eats snails, shrimp, small fish and other crayfish
Omnivore: sinking crayfish/shrimp pellets, algae wafers, frozen foods, a little blanched vegetable
Northern Mexico and the south-central/southeastern US; introduced worldwide
notes: Hard water (8–15 dGH) and extra calcium help it molt.
Uproots and shreds live plants: go with hardscape and caves.
warn: Never release it outdoors: it is a major invasive species, and some states restrict or ban keeping it.
Escape artist: use a solid lid with every gap sealed.

sources.name: fishstores.org – Red Swamp Crayfish care guide

in-cambarellus-patzcuarensis.title: Dwarf Orange Mexican Crayfish (CPO)
in-cambarellus-patzcuarensis.summary: A tiny crayfish from Lake Pátzcuaro, Mexico, sold in its bright orange aquarium form. Much more peaceful than big crayfish, it can share a tank with small fish, plants and snails.
rows: Quite peaceful; they threaten each other but rarely do harm, and mostly pick off sick animals
Lake Pátzcuaro and nearby springs, Michoacán, Mexico
notes: The orange color is a captive mutation; wild animals are brown.
Babies are tiny: cover the filter intake with sponge.
warn: Endangered in the wild (IUCN): never release.

sources.name: Tropical Fish Hobbyist – The Orange Dwarf Crayfish

in-parasesarma-bidens.title: Red Claw Crab
in-parasesarma-bidens.summary: A small, colorful mangrove crab that is often sold as a freshwater pet but really lives in brackish water and needs dry land to climb out on.
rows: Carapace up to about 2 in; leg span up to about 4 in
10 gal minimum (one male with up to two females)
Territorial: one male with several females; hunts small fish
Omnivorous scavenger: pellets, algae wafers, frozen meaty foods and some vegetable matter or leaf litter
Coastal mangroves of the Indo-Pacific, from Zanzibar to Japan and Fiji
notes: Needs a land area above the water (a paludarium or a lowered water line with décor breaking the surface).
warn: Escape artist: tight lid, and block every cable hole.

in-caridina-typus.title: Australian Amano Shrimp
in-caridina-typus.summary: A small detritus-eating shrimp from coastal streams across the Indo-West Pacific, sold as the "Australian Amano". It shreds leaf litter and cleans up leftovers.
rows: Scavenger: picks at detritus and shreds leaf litter
Tropical Indo-West Pacific, from East Africa to Polynesia: rivers and streams near coasts and on islands
notes: Larvae need salt water to develop, so young will not survive in a freshwater tank.
Hides under rocks by day and forages at night.
